# Quantitative parity bridge mass between simplex-vertex clusters

This note gives a quantitative version of the exact support exclusion in
`candidate 32c90486ff8c59d7`.
The conclusion concerns actual convex-compatible integer fibers. It
controls forced mass between prescribed clusters, and the overlap charge
of a specified canonical cap cover. It does not infer ordinary or mixed
depth lower bounds from a cap-cover upper certificate.

## 1. A finite midpoint transport lemma

Let two finite families of measurable positive-volume sets A_u,B_v in
R^d be indexed by u,v in Z^n, with d>=1. Suppose measurable sets C_w
satisfy

    (A_u+B_v)/2 subset C_(u+v)

for every pair of positive-volume sources. Write A=sum_u |A_u|>0 and
B=sum_v |B_v|>0. Then

    sum_w |C_w| >= Phi_d(A,B),
    Phi_d(A,B)=2^(-d)(A^(1/d)+B^(1/d))^d.                (1)

The sets need only be compact convex in the application below; more
generally it suffices that the displayed Minkowski sums are measurable
and satisfy Brunn--Minkowski.

Here is a direct proof that avoids collisions of target indices. Order
the two finite index sets lexicographically, u_1<...<u_p and v_1<...<v_q.
Partition [0,1] into consecutive intervals I_i of lengths |A_(u_i)|/A
and, separately, intervals J_j of lengths |B_(v_j)|/B. Let

    pi_ij=length(I_i intersect J_j).

The positive pi_ij sum to one. Reading their positive-length overlap
intervals from left to right, both indices i,j are nondecreasing, and
at least one increases strictly between different entries. Lexicographic
order is preserved by addition. Consequently all sums u_i+v_j at
positive entries are distinct. Simultaneous partition endpoints cause
no problem: zero-length overlaps are omitted.

Moreover |A_(u_i)|>=pi_ij A and |B_(v_j)|>=pi_ij B. Brunn--Minkowski and
homogeneity therefore give

    |C_(u_i+v_j)|
       >=2^(-d)(|A_(u_i)|^(1/d)+|B_(v_j)|^(1/d))^d
       >=pi_ij Phi_d(A,B).

Summation over those distinct target bases proves (1). No product order,
rectangular four-point inequality, or independence of coordinates is
used. The lexicographic order is only a way to choose a collision-free
finite coupling. If one total is zero, we use the trivial bound zero;
we do not assert the positive formula in (1) in that case.

## 2. Actual fibers and disjoint bridge regions

Let T be a d-simplex with vertices v_0,...,v_d, barycentric coordinates
lambda_0,...,lambda_d, and centroid g. Select k distinct vertices and put

    Q_i=v_i+delta(T-g),       0<delta<1/2.

Let C be a compact convex body in R^n times R^d, with actual integer
fibers K_z={x:(z,x) in C}. All volumes below are ordinary d-volume;
zero-volume fibers are allowed and contribute zero. Compactness leaves
only finitely many nonempty integer fibers. Define

    U=union_i Q_i,
    a_zi=|K_z intersect Q_i|,
    A_ir=sum_(z congruent r mod 2) a_zi,
    M_i=sum_r A_ir,
    E=sum_z |K_z outside U|,
    M=E+sum_i M_i.

The neighborhoods Q_i are pairwise disjoint. For i!=j define

    R_ij=(Q_i+Q_j)/2=(v_i+v_j)/2+delta(T-g).

Every point in Q_i has lambda_i>=1-delta/(d+1). Every barycentric
coordinate of a point in R_ij is at most 1/2+d delta/(d+1). These
inequalities and delta<1/2 prove R_ij is disjoint from every Q_l.
The regions R_ij for distinct unordered label pairs are also pairwise
disjoint: choose a label in one pair but not the other. Its coordinate
is at least 1/2-delta/(d+1) in the first region and at most
d delta/(d+1) in the second. Their strict gap is 1/2-delta.

For each unordered pair define

    L_ij=max over r with A_ir A_jr>0 of Phi_d(A_ir,A_jr), (2)

with L_ij=0 if no such parity exists. Then the actual bridge mass obeys

    sum_z |K_z intersect R_ij| >= L_ij,
    E >= sum_(i<j) L_ij.                                (3)

To prove the first statement, fix a parity r with both totals positive
and write z=r+2u, w=r+2v. The two source families are K_z intersect Q_i
and K_w intersect Q_j. Actual convexity puts each Minkowski midpoint in

    K_(r+u+v) intersect R_ij.

Apply (1); this gives the bound for that parity, hence its maximum.
The second statement follows by the disjointness of all R_ij outside U.
We do not add the different parity constructions for the same pair:
their target bases or sets could overlap.

In particular, for every distinct i,j and parity with both masses positive,

    E >= Phi_d(A_ir,A_jr) >= sqrt(A_ir A_jr),
    E >= 2^(-d) max(A_ir,A_jr).                          (4)

The geometric-mean inequality follows from the arithmetic--geometric
mean inequality on the two d-th roots. The jump in the second bound
as one positive mass tends to zero reflects the full-dimensional volume
created by Minkowski addition; it must not be extended to a zero source.

There is a useful separate statement for a nonempty null source. If
K_z intersect Q_i contains even one point x, z has parity r, and A_jr>0
for j!=i, fix x and midpoint it with each positive K_w intersect Q_j in
that parity. The target bases (z+w)/2 are distinct as w varies, and the
midpoint sets have volumes 2^(-d)|K_w intersect Q_j|. Thus

    sum_v |K_v intersect R_ij| >= 2^(-d) A_jr.          (4a)

This covers a nonempty zero-volume trace. It gives no conclusion when
the corresponding cluster is absent from that parity entirely.

## 3. Sharpness and quantitative parity stability

The individual-pair bound is sharp on an actual full-dimensional source.
Take n=1 and put fibers Q_i and Q_j at bases -1 and +1. Their Cayley hull
has exactly three integer fibers Q_i,R_ij,Q_j. They all have the same
volume w=delta^d |T|. Thus A_(i,odd)=A_(j,odd)=w, E=w, and equality holds
in (3)-(4). The middle fiber is forced and has positive volume; discarding
it would change the source measure.

Let m=2^n. In each parity class with positive cluster mass choose a
leading label ell_r maximizing A_ir. Let L be the union of these labels,
so |L|<=m. Every nonleading A_ir is at most E, since (4) gives
E>=sqrt(A_(ell_r,r) A_ir)>=A_ir when A_ir>0. Therefore

    sum_(i not in L) M_i <= m(k-1)E,
    sum_(i in L) M_i >= M-[1+m(k-1)]E.                  (5)

One may use fewer than m occupied parities in this bound. Formula (5)
is meaningful when its right side is positive and recovers the exact
at-most-m-label support result at E=0. A finer individual estimate, when
both parity masses are positive, is

    A_ir^(1/d) <= 2E^(1/d)-A_(ell_r,r)^(1/d).           (6)

In particular a leading mass >=2^d E excludes every other positive
label in that parity, since (4)'s root expression is then strictly >E.
No positive-fiber or projected-support location for an ordinary deepest
point is asserted by these estimates.

## 4. A forced charge in the canonical cap cover

Assume d>=2 and also delta<1/d. Let

    H_i={lambda_i>=1/(d+1)},   i=0,...,d.

These closed halfspaces cover all R^d. The cluster Q_i lies wholly in
H_i and misses every H_j with j!=i. Further, R_ij lies in H_i intersect
H_j: both indicated coordinates are at least 1/2-delta/(d+1), which is
strictly greater than 1/(d+1) for the stated parameters. For selected
labels define

    X_i=sum_z |K_z intersect (H_i outside U)|,
    B_i=sum_z |K_z intersect H_i|=M_i+X_i.

The pair-region bounds from (3), disjoint for different pairs, now give

    X_i >= sum_(j!=i) L_ij,
    B_i >= M_i+sum_(j!=i) L_ij.                        (7)

These are actual cap masses of the projected counting measure. They are
lower bounds on the budgets of this particular cover, not lower bounds
on maximal halfspace depth. A different cap family is not constrained
by (7) without a separate geometric argument.

There is also a global overlap bound, using all d+1 canonical caps,
including those attached to unselected vertices. Their multiplicity is
at least one everywhere and at least two on each disjoint R_ij. Thus

    sum_(i=0)^d B_i >= M+sum_(i<j) L_ij.                (7a)

The first M credits all source mass once, including outside mass not
accounted for by the constructed bridges. This can be stronger than
adding only the cluster and bridge terms in (7).

For example, take d=5,n=1 and six equal cluster masses M_i=w>0. For
each label choose a parity carrying at least w/2. Partitioning the labels
by that choice gives group sizes s and 6-s. Every within-group pair has
L_ij>=Phi_5(w/2,w/2)=w/2. Hence (3) gives

    E >= (w/2)[s(s-1)/2+(6-s)(5-s)/2] >= 3w.           (8)

The larger group has at least three labels. By (7), any label in that
group has canonical cap mass at least w+2(w/2)=2w. More strongly for a
larger range of E, (7a) and (8) give

    max_i B_i/M >= (1+3w/M)/6.

In particular, if E<=8w then M<=14w and

    max_i B_i/M >= 17/84 > Gamma_5/2,
    17/84-Gamma_5/2=157/108864>0.                       (9)

In exact form, a canonical cover whose EVERY cap has mass strictly less
than Gamma_5 M/2 necessarily satisfies

    E > (4578/533)w.

Indeed (7a) implies 3w/M<3Gamma_5-1=533/2592, and M=6w+E.

The lower bridge requirement (8) must be retained; an illustration with
E<=w would be impossible already. No realization of every E in the
remaining interval is claimed. Formula (9) is a precise obstruction to
using these canonical six caps for a below-target upper certificate.
It does not establish Gamma_5/2 for all projected counting laws, nor show
a center lies in a positive fiber. Those conclusions require more work.

## 5. Verification

The companion stdlib verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_quantitative_parity_cluster_bridge.py` checks the exact finite
coupling, distinct midpoint bases for several integer dimensions, the
mass inequalities used before taking roots, the barycentric separation
and canonical overlap margins, the sharp actual three-fiber geometry,
and the rational constants. The mathematical proof above, rather than
finite samples, supplies the all-dimensional conclusions.
